title: Plan the Homework Break Before Frustration | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A nine-year-old may push through homework until one difficult problem turns tiredness into an argument. Offering a break only after frustration peaks can make stopping feel like an escape from every challenging question. Pause before work begins and agree on a short break point the child can predict. Try: Finish these three questions, take a five-minute movement break, then return for the last section at this table. A planned pause protects concentration and keeps the parent in a supporting role while the child does the actual work.

claim_limits: Suggested wording is an example, not a guaranteed result.
